module: Mesa Win32 shader cache path handling in the application NVK ICDs
tested_change: Build an absolute extended-length Win32 path during cache creation. Create missing parent directories while preserving drive and UNC roots, and reuse the path for index, blob and temporary-file I/O. The cache file format and namespaces retain their existing keys.

storage_controls.validated: Distinct processes put and retrieved a known payload. Five previously failing directory cases passed per architecture. Both ordinary short paths passed, and an existing ordinary file used as a parent remained a cache miss. Directory components included UTF-16 Chinese characters. The fixture exercised local drive paths.

native_gpu.timing_scope: Initial figures contain one cold and one warm process per image and architecture. Two follow-ups ended without a timed process record. The x86 warm creation time increased in its observed run. The x64 first-pair timings include a host status query overlapping several phases by host and device wall clocks. The warm cache hit count and checked pixel output are the promotion evidence. A steady performance or game FPS improvement remains unverified.

application_selection.arm64ec_runtime: The EC directory runs the x64 control executable with an app-local ARM64EC D3D9 DLL and the x64 Vulkan loader/ICD.

additional_unexpected_restarts.measurement: A 16-process follow-up was dispatched after the functional drawing controls. Only its pre-delay scheduling marker survived. No timed process or image can be assigned to this event.

All registration and D3D9 checks finished. A later SSH dispatch timed out. Its script reached the device, but no focused result directory, native startup marker or completed process record was found after reboot. It supplies no repeat timing.

firmware_reset_evidence.scope: Both SD Hekate payload copies matched the public release byte for byte. The on-card Nyx binary differed from that release. Its early hardware initialization saves SCRATCH200 and the PMC reset source in bootloader variables and then clears SCRATCH200 and writes POR to the reset source. A subsequent Windows read of the register cannot classify the preceding reset by itself. The precise source of the observed restarts was not captured.
